classification.difficultyReason: Identify corresponding vertices and combine marked givens with shared sides, vertically opposite angles or alternate angles.

content.prompt: Use an appropriate test to identify a pair of congruent triangles in each of the figures below.

spec.description: Inverted triangle with a shared central side; one-tick outer sides and two-tick upper half-sides.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}AB&=CB &&\text{(given)}\\AM&=CM &&\text{(given)}\\MB&=MB &&\text{(shared side)}\end{align*}$
Therefore, $\triangle AMB\cong\triangle CMB$ by SSS.

spec.description: Two triangles meet at crossing A; corresponding diagonal segments carry one and two ticks.
spec.mathematics: CA=AD; BA=AE; C,A,D and B,A,E are collinear.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}AB&=AE &&\text{(given)}\\\angle BAC&=\angle EAD &&\text{(vertically opposite angles)}\\AC&=AD &&\text{(given)}\end{align*}$
Therefore, $\triangle ABC\cong\triangle AED$ by SAS.

spec.description: Inverted triangle, two right-angle marks at M and two equal angles labelled theta at B. Source blue fills are replaced by unfilled angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: Angle ABM=angle CBM=theta; angle AMB=angle CMB=90 degrees; BM shared.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\angle ABM&=\angle CBM &&\text{(given)}\\BM&=BM &&\text{(shared side)}\\\angle AMB&=\angle CMB=90^\circ &&\text{(given)}\end{align*}$
Therefore, $\triangle AMB\cong\triangle CMB$ by ASA.

spec.description: Parallelogram-shaped quadrilateral with diagonal BD and matching single/double parallel marks.
spec.mathematics: BA parallel CD; BC parallel AD; BD shared.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\angle ABD&=\angle CDB &&\text{(alternate angles, }BA\parallel CD\text{)}\\BD&=DB &&\text{(shared side)}\\\angle ADB&=\angle CBD &&\text{(alternate angles, }AD\parallel CB\text{)}\end{align*}$
Therefore, $\triangle BAD\cong\triangle DCB$ by ASA.

spec.description: Upright triangle with equal outer sides and equal theta angles at B. No midpoint or right-angle marks. Decorative sector fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: AB=CB; angle ABM=angle CBM; BM shared.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}AB&=CB &&\text{(given)}\\\angle ABM&=\angle CBM &&\text{(given)}\\BM&=BM &&\text{(shared side)}\end{align*}$
Therefore, $\triangle ABM\cong\triangle CBM$ by SAS.

spec.description: Opposite right triangles with vertical BD and horizontal EC meeting at A; matching hypotenuses and vertical legs.
spec.mathematics: ED=CB; AD=AB; angle BAC=90 degrees and angle EAD vertically opposite.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\angle EAD&=\angle CAB=90^\circ &&\text{(vertically opposite angles)}\\ED&=CB &&\text{(given hypotenuses)}\\AD&=AB &&\text{(given sides)}\end{align*}$
Therefore, $\triangle EAD\cong\triangle CAB$ by RHS.

spec.description: Bow-tie triangles with one-tick CA and AD and equal theta angles at B and E. Source sector fills omitted.
spec.mathematics: CA=AD; angle CBA=angle AED; vertically opposite angles at A.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\angle AED&=\angle ABC &&\text{(given)}\\\angle EAD&=\angle BAC &&\text{(vertically opposite angles)}\\AD&=AC &&\text{(given)}\end{align*}$
Therefore, $\triangle EAD\cong\triangle BAC$ by AAS.

spec.description: Upright triangle with equal hypotenuses and right-angle squares on both sides of BM at M.
spec.mathematics: AB=CB; angle AMB=angle CMB=90 degrees; BM shared.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\angle AMB&=\angle CMB=90^\circ &&\text{(given)}\\AB&=CB &&\text{(given hypotenuses)}\\BM&=BM &&\text{(shared side)}\end{align*}$
Therefore, $\triangle AMB\cong\triangle CMB$ by RHS.

spec.description: Opposite right triangles along vertical CAD and diagonal EAB; matching diagonal hypotenuses.
spec.mathematics: EA=AB; angle EDA=angle BCA=90 degrees; vertically opposite angles at A.
spec.answerVisibility: No additional side or angle givens.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\angle EDA&=\angle BCA=90^\circ &&\text{(given)}\\\angle EAD&=\angle BAC &&\text{(vertically opposite angles)}\\EA&=BA &&\text{(given)}\end{align*}$
Therefore, $\triangle EAD\cong\triangle BAC$ by AAS.

spec.description: Quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal BD and opposite sides marked equal by single and double ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Equality marks only; no inferred parallel marks.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}AD&=CB &&\text{(given)}\\DB&=BD &&\text{(shared side)}\\AB&=CD &&\text{(given)}\end{align*}$
Therefore, $\triangle ADB\cong\triangle CBD$ by SSS.
